title: Redundant Copyright and License Boilerplate per Code Block
pattern: License and copyright block comments placed immediately above individual structs, classes, or routines rather than at the file level.
why_bad: Visual clutter. Copyright notices must not obstruct the reading of core interfaces. Standard licensing belongs in file-level headers or a single global file, never repeated in the body of source code.
detection: Standard license terms, copyright marks, or legal disclaimers appearing in comments that do not start at line 1 of the source file.
counterexample: A single file-level license header at line 1, mandated by legal compliance, with no repetition per item.
fix: Remove the inline legal block; rely on project-level `LICENSE` files and file-level header templates.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 4 ("Legal Comments"), Chapter 17 (C1: "Inappropriate Information").
